seo.title: Ask Maps Appointments: What Local Businesses Need
seo.meta_description: Ask Maps appointments let people find open beauty, pet care, auto and home repair slots, and Maps can call businesses. What Orange County owners should do.

h1: Ask Maps Appointments: Google Maps Can Now Find Open Slots and Call Local Businesses
answer: Ask Maps appointments are a new Google Maps feature, launched November 16, 2026, that finds open beauty, pet care, auto and home repair appointments online and can call local businesses for the customer. It is launching first in the U.S. Anaheim and Orange County businesses in those categories should make sure their booking links, hours and phone details are accurate.
key_takeaways: Covers beauty, pet care, auto and home repair appointments.
Ask Maps can call local businesses for customers.
Finding appointments launches first in the U.S.
Accurate booking links, hours and phones decide who gets the booking.

sections.heading: What Google announced
sections.body_html: On November 16, 2026, Google launched new Ask Maps features for the holidays. Among them, Google says Ask Maps can now find beauty, pet care, auto and home repair appointments online and call local businesses for you, using what it calls new agentic capabilities.

sections.heading: How it works for customers
sections.body_html: Google's example is simple: a person asks for a 4 p.m. nail appointment nearby, and Ask Maps shows open slots across nearby businesses so it is easy to decide what to book.

sections.heading: Where it is available
sections.body_html: Google says finding appointments, along with route tips, is launching first in the U.S., with more regions coming. Ask Maps itself is expanding to 30 countries in Europe, reaching more than 200 countries and territories.

sections.heading: Why this matters for local businesses
sections.body_html: Until now, a customer usually searched, compared a few profiles and then called or booked. Ask Maps now does part of that work for them, so the businesses it can check, because their availability and contact details are clear, are the ones that get considered.

sections.heading: Which Orange County businesses it affects first
sections.body_html:
• Nail, hair, lash and beauty salons.
  • Groomers, pet sitters and other pet care.
  • Auto repair, tires and detailing.
  • Home repair trades such as plumbing, electrical and handyman services.

sections.heading: Check your booking link
sections.body_html: If you take appointments online, make sure your Google Business Profile links to the booking page you actually use, and that it shows real availability. A dead link or a page that only says call us gives Maps nothing to show.

sections.heading: Check your phone and hours
sections.body_html: Because Ask Maps can call local businesses for customers, a phone number that goes to a full voicemail, or hours that are wrong, can lose the booking. Update holiday hours early and make sure calls are answered or returned quickly.

sections.heading: Make services clear
sections.body_html: List each service you offer on your profile and website in plain words, such as gel manicure, dog grooming for large breeds or brake inspection. A customer asks for a specific service, and Maps can only match it if you name it.

sections.heading: Reviews still matter
sections.body_html: When several businesses have open slots, customers still choose by rating and reviews. Steady, genuine reviews that mention the service help you win the choice.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Check the booking link on your Business Profile.
  2. Confirm hours, including Thanksgiving and December.
  3. List every service by name.
  4. Answer calls or set up quick callbacks.
  5. Ask recent customers for reviews.

sections.heading: A worked example
sections.body_html: Imagine a nail salon in Fullerton whose profile links to an old booking app. The owner switches the link to the current booking page, lists each service with prices, adds holiday hours and asks for reviews after each visit. When someone nearby asks Ask Maps for a 4 p.m. appointment, the salon's open slots can now be shown.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask whether they need a special integration. Google's post doesn't describe one for businesses, so start with what you control: an accurate profile, a working booking link and answered phones. Another common question is whether this replaces their booking software. It doesn't; it sends customers to the systems and phones you already use. Owners also ask whether small, one-chair businesses benefit. They can, because Ask Maps compares nearby availability, not just size.

sections.heading: Keep Apple Maps and your website consistent
sections.body_html: Customers also use Apple Maps and your website. Keep hours, phone and booking links the same everywhere, so any assistant or app that checks your details finds the same answer. Inconsistent details make it harder for any of them to recommend you with confidence.

sections.heading: Prepare staff for AI-assisted calls
sections.body_html: If Ask Maps calls on a customer's behalf, the call may be short and specific: a service, a time and a name. Brief whoever answers the phone to confirm availability clearly and take the booking the same way they would for any caller, so the appointment is not lost to confusion.

sections.heading: Track where bookings come from
sections.body_html: Add a question at booking, such as how did you find us, or use your booking software's source reports, and watch for growth from Google Maps over the holiday season. This tells you whether the effort on your profile is paying off.

sections.heading: Getting your booking page ready
sections.body_html: Open your booking page on a phone, as a customer would, and try to book a common service at a common time. Count the taps, note anything confusing and fix it: unclear service names, required account sign-ups, or availability that only shows a week at a time. Make sure each service shows a duration and a price or price range, and that cancellations and deposits are explained in one sentence. A booking page that is fast and clear on a phone helps every customer, including those who arrive through Ask Maps or any other app.

sections.heading: What to do if you don't take online bookings
sections.body_html: Many Orange County trades still book by phone, and that's fine. Make sure the phone number on your profile is the one that rings where someone answers, set clear hours for calls, and turn on a short voicemail greeting that says when you'll call back. If you use a call-answering service during busy months, give it your service list and typical availability, so it can confirm appointments accurately. Phone-first businesses can still win these searches if calls are handled quickly and politely.

sections.heading: Holiday timing
sections.body_html: The holidays are when people book the most last-minute appointments, from haircuts before family gatherings to car repairs before road trips. Publish extended or reduced hours early, open extra slots where you can, and keep a short waitlist for cancellations. Post a Business Profile update about holiday availability, and reply to messages within a few hours. These small steps help you capture demand when people are searching most.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Ask Maps can now find appointments and call local businesses in the U.S. Anaheim and Orange County salons, pet care, auto and home repair businesses should check booking links, hours, phones, service names and reviews now, before the holiday rush.
